# dsh-complex-project-preset
**An agent preset for DeepSeek Harness (DSH): the full standard tool stack, plus the discipline to t
hink before it types.**
> 中文版: README.zh.md
The whole preset lives in `cordis.patch.yml`: it inserts one `@deepseek-ai/dsh-agent-preset` row int
o the profile and registers a preset with the id `complex-project`. The package ships **configuratio
n only** — no host code, no browser UI — so there is very little that an upgrade can break.
## Why
The standard preset gets work done, but it will not hold a line on its own: diffs creep, project doc
s turn into changelogs, and code goes up before you said so.
This preset writes four rules into the persona prompt, so every session starts with them already in
reset writes four rules into the persona prompt, so every session starts with them already in force:
| Rule | In one line |
| Four documents | A project keeps at most four docs: intro, decisions, change log, current state &

next steps |
| Current state only | No AI edit history, no superseded decisions, no leftover "stage

1–5" wording |
| Commit/push red line | No `git commit`, `git push`, or PR until you explicitly say

so |
| Careful coding + plain language | Restate the goal and the done-criteria first, make surgical
diffs, lead reports with the conclusion |
## What's inside
The tool stack matches the standard preset — bash/pwsh chosen per platform, file read/write and sear
ch, tasks and background jobs, skills, plan mode, compaction, subagents and workflows, web fetch, th
e TODO tool, present. What differs is the persona prompt and the documentation rules:
- `persona` — the four-document policy, current-state-only docs, the commit/push red line, the caref

ul-coding rules, and plain-language reporting;
- `agent-instructions` — still loads your global `AGE

NTS.md` (64 KB cap);
- `planning` / `compaction` / `delegation` — same groups and isolation settings

as standard;
- `tool-plugin-manager` — disabled, so the agent cannot rewrite its own plugin tree.
> ⚠️ The persona block deliberately sets **no `suffix`**. DSH registers only `provider` and `model`
as prompt variables; any other `{{name}}` throws during prompt assembly and the whole turn fails bef
ore a single request is sent. The working directory is injected by the runtime context already, so d
eclaring it here is redundant as well as fatal.
## Install
[代码示例省略，未执行]
**Restart the profile** (run `dsh web` again, or restart the desktop app) — a preset is a row in the
profile composition, not a runtime hot-load.
Uninstall: `dsh plugin --profile web remove dsh-complex-project-preset`
### Conflicts with a hand-rolled copy
If your profile's `cordis.patch.yml` already declares `- id: preset-complex-project` by hand, instal
ling this package registers the same preset twice and DSH reports `Duplicate agent preset: complex-p
roject`. To switch over:

1. delete that `- id: preset-complex-project ...` block from your `cordis.patch.yml`;
2. `dsh plugin

--profile <name> add dsh-complex-project-preset`;
3. restart the profile.
Only one package should provide `complex-project` at a time.
### Version requirement
Requires **DSH ≥ 0.1.7-rc.2** (the preset registry `@deepseek-ai/dsh-agent-preset-registry` joins th
e base composition there) and **Node.js ≥ 22.19.0**. Verified on DSH 0.1.7-rc.2 and on the desktop b
on there) and **Node.js ≥ 22.19.0**. Verified on DSH 0.1.7-rc.2 and on the desktop build 0.2.1-rc.2.
The Node floor is the harness's own rather than this package's: DSH compositions call `process.getBu
iltinModule`, which Node ships from 22.3 onwards. This package is a manifest plus one YAML patch — n
o host code, no browser code, no install-time scripts — so it never loads JavaScript of its own, and
the floor only mirrors where DSH can run at all.
## Verify
After a restart, open the mode picker for a new session: **复杂项目模式** (order 2, right after the standa
rd preset) should be listed. Start a session with it and ask about the project's current state — the
answer should talk in terms of the four documents rather than freeform.
From the CLI you can also inspect the composed tree:
[代码示例省略，未执行]
## Develop
[代码示例省略，未执行]
`tools/smoke.mjs` verifies that `dsh.bundle.patch` points at a file that exists, that `repository` p
oints back at this repo, that every required preset field is present, that child row ids are unique,
and that the persona prompt is neither truncated nor carrying a stray `suffix`. It parses the patch
with the harness's own `loadOverlayPatches` when available, so `!!js` expressions behave exactly as
's own `loadOverlayPatches` when available, so `!!js` expressions behave exactly as they do at boot.
